environment.description: Same CI/CD runner plugin deployed on an ephemeral Buildkite agent with process-level confinement. The agent bootstrap script invokes the plugin binary via `unshare --mount --pid --fork chroot /opt/pipeline-sandbox/ /usr/bin/python3 app.py` where /opt/pipeline-sandbox is a minimal root containing only the Python runtime, the application code, and an empty /var/pipeline/cache directory. The chroot target directory has no /var/pipeline/secrets mount (the directory exists but is empty - secrets are injected only as environment variables to the parent process, not propagated into the chroot namespace). The /etc/resolv.conf inside the chroot points to a local dnsmasq instance that only resolves the GraphQL endpoint hostname to 127.0.0.1. Additionally, the process runs under a dedicated UID (65534/nobody) with a RLIMIT_NPROC of 1 preventing subprocess spawning, meaning the curl-based execute_query() function will fail with OSError when attempting subprocess.run(). The combination means: (1) no secrets files readable inside the chroot, (2) no subprocess execution possible so GraphQL injection via curl cannot reach the backend, (3) DNS resolution restricted to prevent SSRF to other internal services.

config.secrets_injection: env-vars to parent only, not propagated to chroot child
config.dns_resolution: local dnsmasq, only resolves graphql hostname to 127.0.0.1
